author: Terrell Boettcher
title: April 7 election to feature local board candidates - NewsBreak
text:
By Terrell Boettcher ,
23 hours ago The spring election will be held Tuesday April 7 in Sawyer County and throughout Wisconsin, featuring candidates for local school boards, town, city and village governing boards. Polling places will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
There is one state-wide race, for Wisconsin Supreme Court Justice, between Chris Taylor and Maria S. Lazar.
Locally, there will be an operational funds referendum in the Winter School District (see separate article).
The local candidates are as follows
Hayward Community School Board, two open positions. The candidates are Chad Springer and Jared Shuman. Incumbents Dr. Harry Malcolm and Shane Poppe did not file for re-election.
The winners in the April 7 election will serve three-year terms on the Hayward School Board.
Hayward City Council: Those who have filed as candidates for the alderperson districts are:
District 1—Joe Kreyer (incumbent);
District 2—Ken Disher; incumbent Dena Herrman is not running;
District 3—No one filed as a candidate, including incumbent Mike Swan. Individuals can register with the city clerk as a write-in. Voters can write in the name of a candidate. If no one is elected, then the mayor will appoint someone to serve in the position.
District 4—Jim Miller, incumbent.
Sawyer County Board
All 15 seats on the Sawyer County Board of Supervisors are up for election on April 7. The candidates who filed to represent the various supervisory districts are:
District 1: Steve Kariainen, incumbent.
District 2: Kay M. Wilson, incumbent.
District 3: Tweed Shuman (incumbent) and Steve R. Longtime.
District 4: Stacey Hessel, incumbent.
District 5: Randy Neumann, incumbent.
District 6: Marc D. Helwig, incumbent.
District 7: Jim Miller. Incumbent Thomas W. Duffy filed a noice of noncandidacy.
District 8: Marshall Savitski, incumbent.
District 9: Jim Evans, incumbent.
District 10: Chuck Van Etten, incumbent.
District 11: Jeff Hoehne, incumbent.
District 12: John Righeimer, incumbent.
District 13: Ron Kinsley, incumbent.
District 14: Ron Buckholtz, incumbent.
District 15: John Minto. Incumbent Dale Magnuson filed a notice of non-candidacy.
Townships
Area townships with five-member governing boards (chairperson plus four supervisors) will elect two supervisors each on April 7. The candidates are:
Bass Lake: Jim Evans (incumbent), Kevin O. May, Jerry Bond Sutton. Incumbent Dave Aubart is not running for re-election.
Hayward: There are three candidates: Carol Williamson and Brenda Dettloff (both incumbents) and Donald Hamblin.
Lenroot: Rob Mittlesdorf and Jason Sjostrom (incumbent). Incumbent Brett Danielson is not running.
Round Lake: Daniel Palmer and Marvin (Scott) Verbeck, both incumbents.
Spider Lake: Bill Amery and David Thearin, both incumbents.
Winter School Board, Area 5: Michael Kinsley, Taylor Engholm (write-in).
Birchwood School District: Rebecca Hrdlicka.
Village of Couderay: Dennis Zajac.
Village of Exeland: Nicole Trott.
Village of Radisson: Susan A. Spayer.
Village of Winter: Jennifer Holm.
